outcome.technical: ATTEMPT 3 - the adversarial review's findings, each with a case red on the attempt-2 code, and its probes (p1-p8, under <scratchpad>) re-run. H1+H2 (one fix): git's exit no longer decides a move. After `git checkout -q --detach <head>` the tree must answer as the work and nothing else (_worktrees._answers_as): HEAD is the head; `status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=all --no-renames` lists exactly the work paths (a work file the head's .gitignore hides is 'no longer listed'; a file git could not update is 'changed though not the task's'); `diff --name-only <head>` names nothing outside the work; each work path reads back byte for byte. Otherwise the move is undone. The undo ALWAYS goes back to the base (`checkout -q -f --detach <base>`), puts the git index back from the copy (the copy now holds the index file too), writes every held path back even when git's half fails (a forced checkout that stops on one file has already overwritten others - av15 found this in my own first version), and is itself checked by _answers_as against the pre-move state; `restored` is that check, never git's exit; a failed one keeps and names the copy with what is still wrong (av26). Ignored file where the head starts tracking one (review's P1b): refused by name before anything is written (_occupied over the paths `diff --name-status` marks added, read under the name the filesystem holds them by, so a case-only rename on a case-folding filesystem is not a false refusal - av25). M1: the copy records its move (from, to, work, moved); advance_task_tree reads a leftover copy first (_resume): a tree that already answers as that move's result is finished (marker brought to it, `resumed` True, no second checkout); any other is undone back to the base and the copy dropped; an unreadable copy, or one taken from a base the marker does not name, stops with the copy named. M2: drive-phase.advance_member computes the record paths with _invariants.record_rels (union the wave's cached ones), so a tree adopted by a later wave holding refreshed records is not refused as overlapping. L1: the copy is claimed with os.mkdir; FileExistsError never deletes a copy this mover did not make (av21, the review's p5 race). L3: write_record serialises first and writes through _write_aside (mkstemp temp name in the target's directory, os.replace, temp removed on failure), and the recorded move lists the files that moved under the work, the caller's records left out (av22); the journal row does the same. L5: the index is part of the copy and is restored on every undo (av18). The review's note on av9: av9's refused checkout now runs the full undo (checked), and av16 exercises a checkout that ran and then gave no answer. wq2 tightened: besides the unmoved files being byte-identical, every non-record file the phase moved under the member's tree must now hold the head's bytes (src/f1.txt is among them, so the check is not empty). Records in the index: a record not at the base is taken out of the index (`rm --cached --ignore-unmatch`) as well as the working tree (av17, the review's p7). LINT TABLES (tools/lints/_deps.py): the listings moved into one helper, _tree_paths, so the GIT_PATH_BASE_EXEMPT row now names it (the advance_tree row would be stale); a STATE_WRITERS row for _worktrees._write_aside (binary index + marker, _manifest_io's writer is a layer-mate, mkstemp temp name). PROBES RE-RUN (<scratchpad>/p1..p8): p1 advanced=False, error names gen/new_module.py, status still `?? gen/new_module.py`; p1b refused, local.cfg keeps the tree's bytes; p2 DF1/DF2/CASE refused by git and restored (checked), CASE2 (case-only rename) advances, EXEC/SYMLINK/CRLF advance with bytes intact; p3 the next step finishes the killed move (advanced=True) and a later move then runs; p4 advanced=False restored=True, HEAD at base, status ` M a.txt`, m_first.txt base bytes; p5 cannot run unchanged (it wraps _keep_copy with a two-argument function and _keep_copy now takes four) - av21 is the same race with a signature-agnostic wrapper; p7 advanced=True with only `M  a.txt` left; p8 unchanged (fifo not listed by git; an unreadable file would raise from _snap - not addressed, noted). MUTATION TABLE (scratch copy, anchors asserted to land once, pycache purged; <scratchpad>/probe/mutations3.py + mutations3b.py, outputs probe3.log, probe5.log): tree not checked after checkout -> av7 av13 av15 av24; ignored-work not noticed -> av13; unupdated file not noticed -> av15 av24; ignored file where head tracks not refused -> av14; on-disk name not read -> av25; undo not to the base -> av16 av24; index not put back -> av18; record left in the index -> av17; leftover copy never read -> av19 av20; finished move undone and redone -> av19 (after av19 pinned `resumed`; the first run showed this row surviving and the case was tightened); another mover's copy deleted -> av21; records in the recorded move -> av22; marker written in place -> av23; undo claims restored unchecked -> av26; undo returns before writing back -> av26; drive reads only cached records -> ab5; byte check skipped -> av7; forced checkout + no check -> av2; overlap ignored + forced + no check -> av4; copy kept after clean undo -> av8; marker not rewritten -> av19 av22 tv1 tv2 ab3; drive never moves -> ab1 ab2 ab3 ab5. Attempt-1 rows whose anchors survive, re-run (probe4.log): overlap never computed -> av3 av5 tv3 (av4, ab4 survive: git refuses the same overlap); checkout forced -> av1; records as work -> av6 av12; HEAD-is-base dropped -> av11; already dropped -> av10; no journal row -> ab2; refused checkout read as a move -> av9; another task's marker -> tv4; refused move not said -> ab4. GATES RUN, each exit 0: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__worktrees.py tests/test_drive_phase.py` (2/2 files ok, 719 cases); test__worktrees 139/139; test_manage_worktrees 74/74; test_drive_phase 580/580; test__filed_returns 117/117; test__deps 254/254; test__output_lints 169/169; ruff check and vermin -t=3.8- over the changed files. NOT DONE: a work file the process cannot read (mode 000) makes _snap raise an uncaught PermissionError out of advance_tree before anything is written (the review's p8) - the tree is untouched but the drive would see a traceback, not a refusal; the move is skipped on a platform where chmod does not stop a write (av15/av24 skip by the mechanism, as _harness.skip requires). DEPENDANTS: unchanged from attempt 2 except tools/lints/_deps.py (two table rows, no name or layer changed; its importers evals.json, _manifest_rules, _manifest_vocab, _doctor_policy, test__deps, test__manifest_vocab, test__output, test__panel_paths still correct) and _worktrees.py (new private helpers only; the eight importers keep every existing name and behaviour; integrate-task.py reads the marker base, which a resumed move now also brings up to date); the module map fence is unchanged (only stdlib tempfile was imported; g1 green).
outcome.descriptive: The tree mover now judges a move by what the tree holds afterwards, undoes anything else back to the base with bytes and index, refuses ignored files in the way, finishes or undoes a move a killed process left, and the drive knows its record paths before the first refresh.
